npcs.name: Mayor Haldrin Moth
npcs.description: A town mayor rooted at the council chamber and festival platforms, known for how he clears his throat before every compromise.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Mayor is already at the council chamber and festival platforms, working as a town mayor with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on his fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: he clears his throat before every compromise. Close by sits his prized chain of office that pinches when he lies, a small anchor in a loud town. Patronized by Edric; depends on Penna; peers with Sava. He wants to leave town richer in goodwill than coin. He fears a scandal collapsing Midsummer trade more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails him: Accepted Edric's festival funding with fewer questions than Penna liked.
npcs.personality: Steady and sharp-eyed; clears his throat before every compromise.
npcs.motivation: To leave town richer in goodwill than coin without feeding a scandal collapsing Midsummer trade.
npcs.secret: Knows more about this than he admits: Accepted Edric's festival funding with fewer questions than Penna liked.
npcs.rumor: Mayor can open doors at the council chamber and festival platforms after hours—if asked the right way.
npcs.voice: Low and practical, with a habit of repeating the important clause once.
npcs.appearance: A human silhouette framed by the council chamber and festival platforms, hands seldom empty of the chain of office that pinches when he lies.

relationships.note: Cannot run council paperwork without Penna.

npcs.name: Penna Ledgerwell
npcs.description: Penna holds down the records hall with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Walk into the records hall and you will find Penna Ledgerwell before you find a free chair. A 32-year-old Human town clerk, Penna greets trouble the way other folk greet weather: with a coat and a plan. She alphabetizes emergencies. The ribbon tags for 'urgent', 'political', and 'do not lose' travels with her almost everywhere. Essential to Mayor; threat to Orin; overflow to Hala. Her ambition is to digitize nothing and perfect everything on paper. Her nightmare is forged seals passing her desk. Right now, Flagged a warehouse writ with Pale Orin's distinctive pen pressure.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; alphabetizes emergencies.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to digitize nothing and perfect everything on paper.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Flagged a warehouse writ with Pale Orin's distinctive pen pressure.
npcs.rumor: A smugglers' mark was seen near the records hall on a night Penna worked late.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the ribbon tags for 'urgent', 'political', and 'do not lose'.

relationships.note: Cannot run council paperwork without Penna.

npcs.name: Bailiff Crowe
npcs.description: Familiar face at collection rounds and holding cells; useful, stubborn, and hard to surprise.
npcs.biography: Bailiff did not plan to become the town's go-to bailiff, yet collection rounds and holding cells made the choice sticky. Now 48, the Human measures success in quiet evenings and unpaid favors returned. He recites fine schedules like scripture, and keeps the baton he has never raised and always shows like a confessor keeps secrets. Works with Judge Sava; pressured by alleys. Hope pulls one way—enforce law without starring in Kitty's rumors—while caution pulls the other because of becoming Marrow's public face. Was offered a bribe to 'misplace' Rook's holding paperwork.
npcs.personality: Proud of competence more than praise; recites fine schedules like scripture.
npcs.motivation: Protect his place at collection rounds and holding cells long enough to enforce law without starring in Kitty's rumors.
npcs.secret: Has not told allies that was offered a bribe to 'misplace' Rook's holding paperwork.
npcs.rumor: Someone paid Bailiff to forget a name connected to collection rounds and holding cells.
npcs.voice: Measured human cadence; concrete nouns before adjectives.
npcs.appearance: Work-worn human garb; baton he has never raised and always shows always nearby.

npcs.name: Miln Tallcount
npcs.description: Miln holds down doorsteps with a counting board with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Miln Tallcount's reputation as a tax assessor was built one careful errand at a time around doorsteps with a counting board. Age 53 sits lightly on this Halfling, except when old debts creak. Watch long enough and you will see that he apologizes and assesses in the same breath. The folding abacus and a rainproof satchel is part tool, part talisman. Unpopular; useful against Nedda; supports Bera. He would trade sleep to fund Bera's second well through honest tallies, yet stays wary of being drowned in a well 'accident' of popularity. Current spark: Found undeclared barge income patterns matching Nedda's trips.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; apologizes and assesses in the same breath.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to fund Bera's second well through honest tallies.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Found undeclared barge income patterns matching Nedda's trips.
npcs.rumor: Miln can open doors at doorsteps with a counting board after hours—if asked the right way.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the folding abacus and a rainproof satchel.

npcs.name: Judge Sava Wren
npcs.description: Local magistrate whose days orbit the magistrate's bench and small lasting loyalties.
npcs.biography: Judge Sava Wren keeps the magistrate's bench running with the stubborn patience of a 61-year-old Half-Elf who has already survived worse seasons than this one. She makes eye contact with the poorest person first, and the gavel with a softened rim is usually within reach when tempers rise. Peer to Mayor; works with Crowe and Merrick. Her private aim is plain enough: set a precedent that ledgers bind lords too. Still, she flinches at the thought of nobles buying outcomes through festival gifts. Lately the trouble under her nose is this: Asked Merrick for a clean chain of evidence on Rook before festival court.
npcs.personality: Dry humor over a careful heart; makes eye contact with the poorest person first.
npcs.motivation: Finish one honest plan: set a precedent that ledgers bind lords too.
npcs.secret: Keeps proof related to a problem—Asked Merrick for a clean chain of evidence on Rook before festival court.
npcs.rumor: The gavel with a softened rim once belonged to a person who vanished upriver.
npcs.voice: Storyteller rhythm even when discussing ledgers or latches.
npcs.appearance: Half-Elf features shaped by work at the magistrate's bench; watch for the gavel with a softened rim.

npcs.name: Bol Brightvoice
npcs.description: Bol holds down corners, steps, and market cries with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Bol is already at corners, steps, and market cries, working as a town herald with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on his fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: he projects news until windows open. Close by sits his prized brass bell with a cracked throat, a small anchor in a loud town. Voice of government; confused by mill intrigue. He wants to be trusted with truth, not only volume. He fears reading a proclamation that starts a riot more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails him: Was handed two conflicting proclamations about mill ownership in one morning.

npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to be trusted with truth, not only volume.

npcs.rumor: Bol can open doors at corners, steps, and market cries after hours—if asked the right way.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the brass bell with a cracked throat.
